Here's a summary of the SRIOV migration test flake review:

The test "SRIOV VMI connected to single SRIOV network migration should be successful with a running VMI on the target" has a history of intermittent failures, mainly in two places: asserting the SR-IOV interface presence in the VMI status and checking for the interface inside the guest VM. The root cause was a delay in the network-info annotation file population via the downward API, which led to migration failures with errors like `context deadline exceeded: file is not populated with network-info` in the virt-launcher pod logs. Sometimes, the SR-IOV interface would disappear from the guest VM after migration, possibly due to NetworkManager issues or interface instability on cold boot [source](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/issues/13648).

This was a product bug, not an infrastructure issue. It was addressed by updating the migration source controller to properly update network interface status during migration (see PRs #15206 and #15226). The test was previously quarantined due to high flakiness but was unquarantined after these fixes were merged, indicating improved stability [source](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/issues/14565).

The quarantine PR for this test has been merged [source](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/pull/15525), and recent changes have improved the test's reliability. If failures persist, continued monitoring or further fixes may be needed, but the main root cause has been addressed. All learnings should be documented in the fix PR as per the flake action plan.

This is a known issue caused by a change in Kubernetes 1.34: the PodObservedGenerationTracking feature is now enabled by default, which requires the ObservedGeneration field in pod conditions. KubeVirt's virt-controller was previously using a JSONPatch that didn't include this field, so when it tried to update the `kubevirt.io/virtual-machine-unpaused` readiness gate, the patch failed. As a result, the readiness gate condition was missing, virt-launcher pods never became Ready, and VMs stayed in a non-ready state—matching the symptoms in your logs ([details](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/issues/15586)).

This issue has been fixed in [PR #15599](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/pull/15599), which switches to a strategic merge patch that works with the new field. The fix is merged and should be included in the latest main branch and recent periodic jobs. If you're still seeing failures, double-check that your test lane is using a commit after 2025-09-08.

The same failures have been observed across multiple 1.34 periodic lanes (sig-operator, sig-compute, sig-network, sig-storage), confirming it's not isolated to this job ([evidence](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/issues/15554), [evidence](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/issues/15527)). The recommended workaround until the fix is present is to use KubeVirt v1.6.0 with Kubernetes v1.33, which is the officially supported combination.

Per the flake action plan, this is a confirmed bug and should be tracked until the fix is verified in CI. If you need to quarantine the test temporarily, use the `[QUARANTINE]` tag and the Quarantine decorator as described in the docs.

The test `[test_id:1651]should result in pod being terminated` failed because the VMI timed out waiting to reach the "Running" phase, remaining in "Scheduling" for 45 seconds on Kubernetes 1.33 ARM64. This kind of flake has been seen before in similar lifecycle tests, often due to intermittent scheduling delays or node readiness issues, especially on ARM64 clusters. The test implementation matches the failure: it waits for the VMI to launch, then expects the pod to terminate after VMI deletion, with a strict 45s startup timeout [source](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/blob/84bae89d9871475270b6baaefb592c5b770b94d5/tests/vmi_lifecycle_test.go).

Recent PRs have changed virt-handler and VMI lifecycle logic, including pod termination and migration handling, which could indirectly affect scheduling and startup on ARM64 [source](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/pull/15540). However, no direct ARM64-specific bug was found.

The recommended next step for non-critical or hard-to-fix flakes like this is to quarantine the test by adding the `[QUARANTINE]` tag and the Quarantine decorator from `tests/decorators/decorators.go` [source](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/blob/84bae89d9871475270b6baaefb592c5b770b94d5/tests/decorators/decorators.go), referencing this issue in the PR. This is a common practice for similar flakes in KubeVirt [source](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/issues/14123).

If further investigation reveals a reproducible bug or infrastructure issue, triage and fix accordingly. Otherwise, quarantine is the preferred mitigation for now.

The 45-second timeout for waiting for a VMI to reach the Running phase is hardcoded and used uniformly across all architectures, including arm64, with no conditional logic for slower platforms. On arm64, this leads to a ~32% failure rate, even though logs show the VMI is scheduled and containers start successfully—indicating the timeout is likely too strict for arm64 environments and not a general bug or infra issue [source](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/blob/9c2c41e64a0979cc3a5920729f9ae8ee03affeb5/tests/vmi_lifecycle_test.go).

There’s precedent for handling arm64-specific flakes by quarantining or skipping tests that fail due to hardware or performance constraints (see ACPI-related test handling in [issue #13501](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/issues/13501) and [PR #13578](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/pull/13578)). The Quarantine decorator is defined in [tests/decorators/decorators.go](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/blob/9c2c41e64a0979cc3a5920729f9ae8ee03affeb5/tests/decorators/decorators.go#L6) and should be used if the test is non-critical or hard to fix immediately.

Given the evidence, the recommended next step is to quarantine the test by tagging it with [QUARANTINE] and applying the Quarantine decorator, referencing this issue in the PR. This is a temporary measure until a more robust solution (like an architecture-specific timeout or deeper arm64 performance improvements) can be implemented [source](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/issues/13868).

If the test is critical for release/blocking, further investigation into arm64 startup performance or increasing the timeout for arm64 lanes may be warranted. Otherwise, quarantining aligns with current KubeVirt flake handling policy.

The AfterSuite flakiness on sig-compute for k8s 1.32 and 1.33 is a known issue, with failure rates up to 22% over 72 hours. These failures are intermittent and often relate to resource cleanup, timing, or cluster state issues during global test teardown. In some cases, logs show "connection refused" errors on localhost API endpoints, suggesting that a test may have destabilized the cluster, leading to AfterSuite failures [example](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/issues/15526).

The recommended process is to review the linked Prow job logs for patterns like repeated cleanup failures or infra slowdowns. If you determine the flake is a bug, label with `/triage accepted`, create a PR to fix it, and keep the issue open until resolved. If it's non-critical or hard to fix, quarantine the test by adding the `[QUARANTINE]` tag to the test name and applying the `Quarantine` decorator from `tests/decorators/decorators.go` [reference](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/blob/c5d0792a4db1586a87ee1a46d1d38d2592433dd2/tests/decorators/decorators.go). If it's an infrastructure issue, label with `/triage infra-issue` and close with details [flake action plan](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/issues/13814).

The Quarantine decorator is used in the codebase as `decorators.Quarantine` and is applied to the test definition (e.g., as an argument to `It` or `Describe` in Ginkgo). Be sure to reference the flake issue in your PR. This approach is well-documented in prior sig-compute flake issues [example](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/issues/13865).

Focus your investigation on resource cleanup, namespace deletion, and cluster profiler teardown in AfterSuite, as these are common sources of flakiness.

This flake is a known issue in the ARM64 compute SIG, affecting about 4% of runs. The test in `vmi_lifecycle_test.go` expects a VirtualMachineInstance with a PanicDevice to crash and enter the Failed phase, but often hits a strict 10-second timeout during console interaction or phase transition. This is likely due to ARM64-specific performance constraints rather than a general bug or infra issue. There is strong precedent in KubeVirt for handling such flakes by quarantining the test using the `[QUARANTINE]` tag and the Quarantine decorator from [`tests/decorators/decorators.go`](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/blob/f85a8117b8a90fd913ec0719faae9506866d1525/tests/decorators/decorators.go#L7), referencing the flake issue in the PR. This approach is recommended unless the test is critical for release, in which case increasing the timeout or deeper ARM64 investigation may be warranted. For more details and similar cases, see [issue #15733](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/issues/15733) and [issue #13501](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/issues/13501).

This flake is a known issue in the ARM64 lanes, where the test expects a pod to transition from `Running` to `Succeeded` within a strict timeout (30s), but on ARM64 hardware, this sometimes doesn't happen fast enough, causing intermittent failures. The test logic itself is generic and not ARM64-specific, but ARM64 performance variability makes these timing-sensitive checks unreliable in CI. Recent issues and PRs confirm similar flakes in `vmi_lifecycle_test.go` on ARM64, with precedent for quarantining such tests using the [Quarantine decorator](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/blob/f85a8117b8a90fd913ec0719faae9506866d1525/tests/decorators/decorators.go#L7) as a temporary measure until a more robust solution (like increasing timeouts or deeper ARM64 investigation) is implemented [[issue #15733](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/issues/15733)].

Recent changes in virt-handler (resource leak fixes in REST lifecycle handlers) improve resource management but do not directly address this pod phase flake [[PR #15582](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/pull/15582)]. The recommended next step, following the KubeVirt flake action plan, is to quarantine the test by tagging it with `[QUARANTINE]` and applying the Quarantine decorator, referencing this issue in the PR. If the test is critical for release, consider investigating ARM64 startup performance or increasing the timeout for ARM64 lanes [[issue #15727](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/issues/15727)].

Let me know if you need more details on the test logic or want to discuss possible timeout adjustments for ARM64.

This test checks that live migration can be canceled by deleting either the source or target migration resource, and expects both migration objects to disappear within 180 seconds. The flake occurs when the migration resource doesn't get cleaned up in time, causing a timeout and a matcher error ("Expected an error, got nil") [source](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/blob/9a6f4a3a707992038ef705da4cb3bba8c89d36ba/tests/migration/namespace.go#L631).

Recent PRs have overhauled migration cancellation: now, deleting either migration resource should propagate cancellation via the synchronization controller, which manages finalizers and sends cancellation requests between source and target [PR #15605](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/pull/15605) [PR #15682](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/pull/15682). A new monitor in virt-launcher was added to poll for the true end of migration jobs and send update events, which may help reduce flakiness [PR #15721](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/pull/15721) [PR #15763](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/pull/15763).

Despite these improvements, the test still fails intermittently—likely due to timing, async propagation, or resource cleanup issues in the controllers. Similar migration flakes have been tracked and quarantined in recent issues [issue #15135](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/issues/15135) [issue #15281](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/issues/15281) [issue #15726](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/issues/15726).

If the flake persists and is hard to fix, the recommended action is to quarantine the test using the `[QUARANTINE]` tag and the Quarantine decorator, referencing this issue in the PR [quarantine process](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/blob/f85a8117b8a90fd913ec0719faae9506866d1525/tests/decorators/decorators.go#L7). This will prevent CI instability while further fixes are investigated.

This type of clustered failure—connection refused to the KubeVirt API endpoint and control-plane not becoming ready within the timeout—is a known issue in periodic sig-compute lanes and has occurred across multiple versions and jobs. The root cause is usually a deployment or infrastructure problem that prevents the control-plane components (like virt-operator, virt-api, or virt-controller) from starting or becoming ready, which cascades into many test failures since the API is unreachable for readiness checks. The test suite fixture code waits for these components to be ready and fails if the 'Available' condition is not true within the timeout, matching the error in your logs [source](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/blob/9a6f4a3a707992038ef705da4cb3bba8c89d36ba/tests/testsuite/fixture.go).

The recommended triage process is well-documented: review the logs for patterns (such as repeated cleanup failures or infra slowdowns), then decide if the flake is a bug (label `/triage accepted` and fix), non-critical/hard to fix (quarantine the test with `[QUARANTINE]` tag and the Quarantine decorator), or an infrastructure issue (label `/triage infra-issue` and close with details) [source](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/issues/15743), [source](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/issues/15526).

If this failure is recurring, it should be tracked and triaged per the flake action plan. If it's a one-off, it may be infra-related and can be closed after review. For infra-related startup delays (like CRI-O socket readiness), mitigations include increasing kubeadm preflight timeouts and adding retries to init/join operations [source](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirtci/issues/1537).

Let me know if you need help interpreting specific logs or want guidance on applying the Quarantine decorator.

This flake is caused by non-deterministic ordering in the migration watcher priority queue when multiple migrations have the same priority. The test expects to dequeue migrations in a specific order (e.g., `default/testmigration0` first), but due to recent changes in the queue logic and the use of equal priorities for active migrations, the dequeue order can vary, especially under concurrent or resource-constrained environments like arm64 CI. This is not an infrastructure issue, nor is it specific to arm64 logic, but rather a race/timing issue in the test or queue implementation itself [[example analysis](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/issues/15726)].

Recent PRs have changed the priority queue logic and constants (now using `pendingPriority = -100` and `activePriority = 100`), and updated the test to check for strict ordering [[PR #15645](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/pull/15645)]. However, the underlying queue does not guarantee order among items with the same priority, leading to intermittent failures like the one observed here [[migration_test.go](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/blob/9a6f4a3a707992038ef705da4cb3bba8c89d36ba/pkg/virt-controller/watch/migration/migration_test.go)].

Given the intermittent nature and difficulty of reliably fixing this quickly, the recommended action is to quarantine the test by adding the `[QUARANTINE]` tag and the [Quarantine decorator](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/blob/f85a8117b8a90fd913ec0719faae9506866d1525/tests/decorators/decorators.go#L7), referencing this issue in the PR. This will prevent the flake from impacting CI stability while a more robust fix is investigated [[flake handling process](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/issues/15743)]. Please monitor for recurrence and revisit after future queue or migration logic changes.

This clustered failure in the periodic-sig-storage lane is caused by an RBAC misconfiguration: the `kubernetes-admin` user lacks permission to get `datavolumes` in the `cdi.kubevirt.io` API group within the `kubevirt-test-default1` namespace. The root cause is likely missing or incorrect RBAC bindings for this user in the test environment, not a bug in the test logic itself. The relevant ClusterRoles grant permissions to service accounts, but not to `kubernetes-admin` by default [rbac-operator.authorization.k8s.yaml](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/blob/main/manifests/generated/rbac-operator.authorization.k8s.yaml.in) [controller.go](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/blob/main/pkg/virt-operator/resource/generate/rbac/controller.go).

Recent changes to the test cluster setup, such as deploying CDI in kind clusters [#15507](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/pull/15507), may have impacted RBAC or resource availability, but the error is not due to missing CDI installation. The RBAC Role created for DataVolume tests only allows `create` on `datavolumes/source` for the `system:authenticated` group, not `get` on `datavolumes` [datavolume.go](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/blob/main/tests/libstorage/datavolume.go).

This matches the pattern of infrastructure issues seen in similar sig-storage failures [issue 14433](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/issues/14433). Per the flake action plan, this should be triaged as an infrastructure issue: add `/triage infra-issue`, close the issue with a comment about the RBAC misconfiguration, and document the fix once resolved. The recommended fix is to update the test setup to grant `kubernetes-admin` the necessary permissions on `datavolumes` in the test namespace.

The error is caused by a configuration requirement in the rules_oci Bazel extension: when the oci_image rule does not specify a base image, both os and architecture must be set explicitly. This was enforced after a recent update to Bazel v6.5.0 and the switch to rules_oci in PR #13111, which changed how these parameters are handled. In the current containerimages/BUILD.bazel, the alpine-container-disk-image rule correctly specifies os and architecture, so if you're still seeing this error, check for typos or missing parameters in any custom or similar image rules that omit base—both os and architecture must be present for those cases. This is a configuration issue, not an infrastructure problem or a transient flake. For reference, see the relevant rule and recent changes [here](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/blob/13822f0db00c56745831c6eb89b6c724cfba451f/containerimages/BUILD.bazel) and [here](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/pull/13111).

The IPv6 flake in the Networking VirtualMachineInstance with masquerade binding mechanism (test_id:1780) started right after the Fedora 39 image update in PR #13322, and only affects the IPv6 lane. This is now being handled by quarantining the affected tests, as documented in PR #15882, following the project's flake action plan.

The root cause appears to be a race condition in the masquerade binding mechanism: TAP interfaces can be removed from the virt-launcher pod before being detached from the VM, which can crash QEMU and cause VM restarts. This is especially problematic in IPv6 scenarios and is exacerbated by KubeVirt's asynchronous architecture between virt-launcher and virt-handler. There is ongoing discussion about improving synchronization and possibly addressing this in both KubeVirt and upstream libvirt/QEMU, with a related PR (#13941) aiming to reduce these race conditions. The masquerade.go implementation itself hasn't changed since before the flake began, so the Fedora 39 image update is the likely trigger for the new failures. 

The tests will remain quarantined until they demonstrate a failure rate of 0.1% or less, at which point they can be dequarantined per the updated process. You can monitor and accelerate this process using the documented dequarantine job and PR workflow. For more details, see [PR #15882](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/pull/15882), [race condition analysis](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/issues/13721#issuecomment-2641959423), and [quarantine process documentation](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/pull/15636).

{"author": "person-0d5c74a9", "base": "main", "body": "### What this PR does
Before this PR:
When using `SafeExpectBatch()` to talk to a guest shell, it's not always practical to expect a prompt after each command, especially when we want to parse command output.
Only one `BExp` is allowed after every `BSnd`, so output parsing and prompt expect need to be conflated into one regex.
In practice, most expecters that parse command output just don't add a prompt expect, and it works just fine in most cases.
However, when timing is just "right", we may:
- Send a command
- Get the expected output
- After the command printed what we wanted and before it finishes, we send the next command
- Our next command is never executed, the expecter fails and the test fails

After this PR:
`SafeExpectBatch()` now always expects a return to prompt before running the next command, eliminating that race.
That means `SafeExpectBatch()` can now only be used in shells to run commands that return to prompt, but that's the vast majority of cases.
The remaining expecters have to use `ExpectBatch()`

{"author": "person-1c8cf47b", "base": "main", "body": "### What this PR does

Delivery of signals can actually drop signal
if multiple signals are generated while the signal is being blocked.
In this case only one signal is delivered after it is un-blocked. Because we always do Wait4 per signal we can actually miss a process being terminated.
Sometimes the ordering happen to be unfortunate and the virt-launcher process is missed and never cleaned up.

This cause for the virt-launcher to hang around indefinitely.

Therefore this commit tries to reap as much processes as possible per signal.

This was observed upon successful migration where both source and target Pods continued to be running, see:
```
ps aux
USER         PID %CPU %MEM    VSZ   RSS TTY      STAT START   TIME COMMAND
qemu           1  0.0  0.0 1679844 13328 ?       Ssl  Aug21   0:00 /usr/bin/virt-launcher-monitor --qemu-timeout 248s --name rhel9-3195 --uid 0db4e8a0-c0e4-4e95-9b1c-bd7f2a16c8d4 --namespace vm-ns-32 --kubevirt-
qemu           8  0.0  0.0      0     0 ?        Z    Aug21  13:51 [virt-launcher] <defunct>
qemu         444  0.5  0.0   4452  2688 pts/0    Ss   09:19   0:00 bash
qemu         445  0.0  0.0   7032  2688 pts/0    R+   09:19   0:00 ps aux

```

and logs:

```
{"component":"virt-launcher","level":"info","msg":"Exiting...","pos":"virt-launcher.go:513","timestamp":"2025-08-29T18:18:58.885293Z"}
{"component":"virt-launcher-monitor","level":"info","msg":"Reaped pid 19 with status 9","pos":"virt-launcher-monitor.go:202","timestamp":"2025-08-29T18:18:58.886212Z"}
{"component":"virt-launcher-monitor","level":"info","msg":"Reaped pid 18 with status 9","pos":"virt-launcher-monitor.go:202","timestamp":"2025-08-29T18:18:58.889628Z"}
```

Links to places where the discussion took place: <!-- optional: slack, other GH issue, mailinglist, ... -->

### Special notes for your reviewer
It is not clear to me if the go runtime suspend the signal (makes it non blocking) before the signal is send to channel and so there is no race.

-->

### What this PR does
When restoring a VM from a VMSnapshot, and if the VM has a regular PVC owned by the VM, the restore would not properly set the owner reference for the restored PVC. This would cause the restored PVC to remain orphaned. Once the user deletes the VM, the restored PVC would not be deleted.

#### Before this PR:
When restoring a VMSnapshot with a regular PVC not owned by a DataVolume, the restored PVC would not be owned by the VM (regardless of the restore policy). The PVC would remain orphaned.

#### After this PR:
If the restore policy is set to VM, then any restored PVCs associated with the VMSnapshot will be owned by the VM. These PVCs will no longer be orphaned when the VM is deleted.

### References
  
- Fixes https://issues.redhat.com/browse/CNV-67307
